name: AmoJS html template
comment: Injects HTML into AmoJS html`` tagged templates. `L:` makes this run BEFORE the host grammar's own template-literal rule, which is the whole reason the injection wins; `-comment -string` keeps it from firing inside a comment or an ordinary quoted string that merely contains the text html`.

template.comment: A TextMate grammar cannot do import analysis, so the `html` tag is matched by name. A foreign html`` (lit-html, a local helper) is highlighted too — accepted: locked rule #8 governs the COMPILER, not the highlighter. The lookbehind rejects `obj.html``, which is never ours.

escape.comment: Must come first: an escaped backtick would otherwise end the template early.
escape.name: constant.character.escape.js

hole.comment: A ${…} hole is JavaScript again. The name is what package.json's embeddedLanguages maps back to javascript, which is what gives completion inside a hole. `include: source.js` is how the host TS grammar does balanced braces, so an object literal consumes its own `}` before the end pattern is tried.
hole.name: meta.template.expression.amojs

tag.comment: We parse tags OURSELVES rather than handing them to text.html.basic, and this is load-bearing. Once the HTML grammar enters a tag it owns that region, and neither an in-grammar `injections` block nor a second grammar injected into text.html.basic gets consulted there (verified against vscode-textmate). The result was that `class=${x}` came out as a plain HTML string: no JS colouring, and — worse — no embedded-language mapping, so no completion inside the hole. Owning the tag is what makes an attribute hole a first-class hole. Tag CONTENT is still text.html.basic's job.
tag.name: meta.tag.amojs.html

attribute.comment: Name first, then let #attribute-value own everything after the `=` — so a static value is a string and a hole is an expression, instead of both being mistaken for another attribute name.

quoted-value.comment: A quoted value may hold a hole — `r="${n}"`, which is also the spelling AmoJS requires when the hole is glued to `/>`.
quoted-value.name: string.quoted.html
